deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: A policy should be set for this to either be PREVENT or ABANDON as this will prevent a user from accidentally deleting an instance.

description.description: An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you create the resource.
description.rationale: No security impact as its purley for the developers to note anything down.

name.description:
The name of the resource, provided by the client when initially creating
the resource. The resource name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply
with RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and
match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])'? which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters
must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character,
which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The name of the resource has no security impact to the resoruces and that the naming convention is usually set by the provider and team.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This specifies the Google Cloud project which contains this resource. A platform policy should not restrict such project identiifiers.

region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

disk_consistency_group_policy.description: Replication consistency group for asynchronous disk replication.

disk_consistency_group_policy.enabled.description: Enable disk consistency on the resource policy.
disk_consistency_group_policy.enabled.rationale: This is up to the developer as disk consistency on the resource does not affect security, by constraining this we are making it difficult for developers.

group_placement_policy.description: Resource policy for instances used for placement configuration.

group_placement_policy.availability_doma.description:
The number of availability domains instances will be spread across. If two instances are in different
availability domain, they will not be put in the same low latency network
group_placement_policy.availability_doma.rationale: This represents the number of VMs in the placement group and therefore does not relate to security

group_placement_policy.collocation.description:
Collocation specifies whether to place VMs inside the same availability domain on the same low-latency network.
Specify 'COLLOCATED' to enable collocation. Can only be specified with 'vm_count'. If compute instances are created
with a COLLOCATED policy, then exactly 'vm_count' instances must be created at the same time with the resource policy
attached. Possible values: ["COLLOCATED"]
group_placement_policy.collocation.rationale: This determines if the VMs will sit in the same low-latency network with the only value being COLLOCATED, this is a functional enum with nothing to contrain and therefore does not have any impacts on security.

group_placement_policy.gpu_topology.description: Specifies the shape of the GPU slice, in slice based GPU families eg. A4X.
group_placement_policy.gpu_topology.rationale: This is functional only and does not have any impact on security.

group_placement_policy.vm_count.description:
Number of VMs in this placement group. Google does not recommend that you use this field
unless you use a compact policy and you want your policy to work only if it contains this
exact number of VMs.
group_placement_policy.vm_count.rationale: This restricts the amount of VMs in the placement group. This does not affect security and it only alters the sizing.

instance_schedule_policy.description: Resource policy for scheduling instance operations.

instance_schedule_policy.expiration_time.description: The expiration time of the schedule. The timestamp is an RFC3339 string.
instance_schedule_policy.expiration_time.rationale: This sets when the start and stop schedule stops applying. This is an operational lifetime for a schedulling job and therefore does not have any impacts on security.

instance_schedule_policy.start_time.description: The start time of the schedule. The timestamp is an RFC3339 string.
instance_schedule_policy.start_time.rationale: This sets when the start time of the instance schedule. This is an operational lifecycle timing and therefore have no security effect.

instance_schedule_policy.time_zone.description:
Specifies the time zone to be used in interpreting the schedule. The value of this field must be a time zone name
from the tz database: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database.
instance_schedule_policy.time_zone.rationale: This sets the time zone of the instance schedule, an misconfigured time zone will simply cause the schedule to run incorrectly and therefore have no security impacts.

instance_schedule_policy.vm_start_schedu.description: Specifies the schedule for starting instances.
Specifies the frequency for the operation, using the unix-cron format.
instance_schedule_policy.vm_start_schedu.rationale: Sets when instances are started and therefore no generic policy can improve security. (operational lifecycle)

instance_schedule_policy.vm_stop_schedul.description: Specifies the schedule for stopping instances.
Specifies the frequency for the operation, using the unix-cron format.
instance_schedule_policy.vm_stop_schedul.rationale: Sets when instances are stopped and therefore no generic policy can improve security. (operational lifecycle)

snapshot_schedule_policy.description: Policy for creating snapshots of persistent disks.

snapshot_schedule_policy.retention_polic.description: Retention policy applied to snapshots created by this resource policy.
Maximum age of the snapshot that is allowed to be kept.
snapshot_schedule_policy.retention_polic.rationale: A generic policy should not be able to set a retention days of the snapshot as this will be too overreaching.

snapshot_schedule_policy.retention_polic.description:
Specifies the behavior to apply to scheduled snapshots when
the source disk is deleted. Default value: "KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS" Possible values: ["KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS", "APPLY_RETENTION_POLICY"]
snapshot_schedule_policy.retention_polic.rationale: This controls what happens to scheduled snapshots when the source disk is deleted with the default being KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS. APPLY_RETENTION_POLICY will mean that destroying the primary disk will also delete its backups. This extra field makes this dangerous as it allows an accidental disk deletion to be unrecoverable. A policy should be written to require KEEP_AUTO_SNAPSHOTS so that the recovery outlives the thing it protects.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.daily_.description: The policy will execute every nth day at the specified time.
Defines a schedule with units measured in days. The value determines how many days pass between the start of each cycle. Days in cycle for snapshot schedule policy must be 1.
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.daily_.rationale: This sets how many days to pass between the snapshots, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.daily_.description:
This must be in UTC format that resolves to one of
00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00, or 20:00. For example,
both 13:00-5 and 08:00 are valid.
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.daily_.rationale: This sets the daily start time for the snapshots should run, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.hourly.description: The policy will execute every nth hour starting at the specified time.
The number of hours between snapshots.
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.hourly.rationale: This sets the number of hours between snapshots, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.hourly.description:
Time within the window to start the operations.
It must be in an hourly format "HH:MM",
where HH : [00-23] and MM : [00] GMT. eg: 21:00
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.hourly.rationale: This sets the hourly schedule start time for the snapshots should run, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.weekly.description: Allows specifying a snapshot time for each day of the week.
May contain up to seven (one for each day of the week) snapshot times.
The day of the week to create the snapshot. e.g. MONDAY Possible values: ["MONDAY", "TUESDAY", "WEDNESDAY", "THURSDAY", "FRIDAY", "SATURDAY", "SUNDAY"]
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.weekly.rationale: This sets the day for the snapshots should run, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.weekly.description:
Time within the window to start the operations.
It must be in format "HH:MM", where HH : [00-23] and MM : [00-00] GMT.
snapshot_schedule_policy.schedule.weekly.rationale: This sets the start time for the snapshots should run, this has no impacts on security.

snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.description: Properties with which the snapshots are created, such as labels.

Creates the new snapshot in the snapshot chain labeled with the
specified name. The chain name must be 1-63 characters long and comply
with RFC1035.
snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.rationale: This is simply an identifier and therefore have no security implications.

snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.description: Whether to perform a 'guest aware' snapshot.
snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.rationale: This does not have an security impact as its more of an backup quality option.
Labels are metadata fro organisation and cost attribution, any policy on this would mean that we will have to name specific keys and therefore does not have any security impact.

snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.description:
Cloud Storage bucket location to store the auto snapshot
(regional or multi-regional)
snapshot_schedule_policy.snapshot_proper.rationale: The cloud storage location of the auto snapshot needs to be controlled. This is due to data sovereignty policies that an organisations may have.

workload_policy.accelerator_topology.description:
The accelerator topology. This field can be set only when the workload policy type is HIGH_THROUGHPUT
and cannot be set if max topology distance is set.
workload_policy.accelerator_topology.rationale: This does not have an security impact as its a peformance topology dictating the accelerator slice shape.

workload_policy.max_topology_distance.description:
The maximum topology distance. This field can be set only when the workload policy type is HIGH_THROUGHPUT
and cannot be set if accelerator topology or accelerator topology mode is set. Possible values: ["BLOCK", "CLUSTER", "SUBBLOCK"]
workload_policy.max_topology_distance.rationale: This does not have an security impact as its a peformance topology dictating the placement distance.

workload_policy.type.description: The type of workload policy. Possible values: ["HIGH_AVAILABILITY", "HIGH_THROUGHPUT"]
workload_policy.type.rationale: There are only two possible values and both values dont have any security impact.
